finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces customer == g.user['id'], which shows the check was intended.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request path parameter inv_id (guessable or enumerable invoice IDs)
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and any other invoice data

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the record by the attacker-supplied ID, with no comparison against g.user
The full invoice is returned as JSON

finding.guards_checked: Searched the whole directory: invoices.py is the only code file. It has no before_request hook, login_required decorator or auth middleware, and the route has no ownership check. The /my/invoice route (lines 16-17) has an ownership check, but this route does not. Any gateway or auth layer outside this repo could not be verified.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, looks up INVOICES.get(inv_id) and returns jsonify(inv) with no g.user comparison, while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 does check inv["customer"] != g.user["id"]; the directory has no other code, so no before_request or middleware guard exists. An external gateway can't be ruled out.

verdict_facts.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator or ownership check and returns jsonify(inv) for any ID, while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 does check inv["customer"] != g.user["id"]; the directory has only this file and no guard.
